```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(scales)
```

## AI assistance disclosure

This report uses AI assistance for structuring the report and preparing R code for tables and plots. 

## Brief description

*Game of Thrones* is an American fantasy drama television series created by David Benioff and D. B. Weiss for HBO. It is based on George R. R. Martin's book series *A Song of Ice and Fire*. The series premiered in 2011 and concluded in 2019 after eight seasons.

## Image

![Title card of *Game of Thrones*. Source: Wikipedia/Wikimedia.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/d/d8/Game_of_Thrones_title_card.jpg)

## Data

The table below shows the number of episodes and the average U.S. viewership for each season, in millions of viewers. Values were taken from the season overview table on Wikipedia.

```{r data}
# AI-assisted code: creates the manually entered viewership table and calculates changes
viewership <- tibble(
  season = 1:8,
  episodes = c(10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 7, 6),
  avg_us_viewers_millions = c(2.52, 3.80, 4.97, 6.84, 6.88, 7.69, 10.26, 11.99)
) %>%
  mutate(
    change_from_previous = avg_us_viewers_millions - lag(avg_us_viewers_millions),
    percent_change = change_from_previous / lag(avg_us_viewers_millions) * 100
  )

viewership %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) %>%
  kable(col.names = c("Season", "Episodes", "Avg. viewers (M)",
                      "Change (M)", "Change (%)"))
```

## Basic statistics

```{r statistics}
# AI-assisted code: calculates basic descriptive statistics from the viewership table
v <- viewership$avg_us_viewers_millions

# Largest and smallest season-to-season changes (season 1 has NA, so skip it)
changes <- viewership %>% filter(!is.na(change_from_previous))
biggest  <- changes %>% slice_max(change_from_previous, n = 1)
smallest <- changes %>% slice_min(change_from_previous, n = 1)

stats <- tibble(
  statistic = c("Min", "Max", "Mean",
                "Season 1 → 8 (absolute)",
                "Season 1 → 8 (percent)"),
  value = c(sprintf("%.2f M", min(v)),
            sprintf("%.2f M", max(v)),
            sprintf("%.2f M", mean(v)),
            sprintf("%+.2f M", v[8] - v[1]),
            sprintf("%+.0f%%",  (v[8] / v[1] - 1) * 100))
)

kable(stats, col.names = c("Statistic", "Value"))
```

Viewership grew every season. Season 1 averaged `r sprintf("%.2f", v[1])` million U.S. viewers; by season 8 the average was `r sprintf("%.2f", v[8])` million — a `r sprintf("%.1f", v[8] / v[1])`× increase over the run of the show.

The biggest jump between consecutive seasons was from season `r biggest$season - 1` to season `r biggest$season` (`r sprintf("%+.2f", biggest$change_from_previous)` million); the smallest was from season `r smallest$season - 1` to season `r smallest$season` (`r sprintf("%+.2f", smallest$change_from_previous)` million).
